Restore element.parent, add element.closest(selector)

v1 exposed DOM navigation via element.parent (and .parent.parent
chains); the v2 rewrite dropped it, so any v1 test walking the DOM
via element accessors broke silently with "cannot read properties of
undefined". Restore parent and add closest(selector) — the native
Element.closest() DOM idiom, robust to markup shuffling.

Both return Element instances with pure-JS locators (null-safe IIFE
wrappers generated by Locators.parentJs / closestJs). Pure-JS locators
already pass through selector() unchanged, so they compose with every
existing element op — waits, script, attribute, chaining — without
touching the CDP or W3C backends.

parent is exposed via jsGet as a direct Element (not a JavaCallable)
so v1-style e.parent.parent chains naturally; closest takes a selector
so it's a callable.

Move the #2803 script() regression scenarios out of their issue-named
feature into a proper "script() and scriptAll() behaviors" section in
element.feature — they describe behavior, not an open bug.

Replace element.parent with closest(selector) + matches(selector)

Pivot the v2 DOM navigation surface to a lean selector-based API that
mirrors the native W3C DOM Element interface:

- remove element.parent (added in the previous commit) — hop-counting
  like e.parent.parent is fragile; a designer wrapping the input in an
  extra <div> silently breaks the test
- keep element.closest(selector) — W3C DOM standard, upward traversal,
  robust to markup shuffling
- add element.matches(selector) — W3C DOM standard, boolean "does this
  element match the selector", complements closest for predicates and
  conditional walks

Together with the existing element.locate / element.locateAll (scoped
descendant lookups) and element.script (escape hatch for arbitrary DOM
walks), this is the complete v2 surface. No parent, no children, no
sibling accessors — if you need them, closest + scoped locateAll or
element.script() cover the cases.

Also fix a pre-existing scoping bug in BaseElement.locate / locateAll
that this new pattern exposes: concatenating the base locator string
with " " + childLocator works for CSS bases but produces invalid JS
when the base is a pure-JS expression (which is what closest returns).
Add Locators.scopedSelectorJs / scopedCountJs / scopedIndexedSelectorJs
helpers and route pure-JS bases through them so closest-then-locateAll
chains actually work.

Also move the #2803 script() regression scenarios out of their issue-
named feature into a "script() and scriptAll() behaviors" section in
element.feature — they describe behavior, not an open bug.

for locate / locateAll, to align with jQuery / Cypress / Selenium naming

Three compounding changes that unblock 264 test262 Array/** tests

  per spec (configurable: true / writable: true). userProps map wins
  over built-in lookups; built-ins themselves remain undeletable.

  Pre-pass binds them before any statement runs; the FN_EXPR is then

  needed when a JsArray sits in a prototype chain (foo.prototype =
  [1,2,3]; new foo() then accesses indices via the chain).
